name: ParseDocument
title: Parse Document
description: Read any document into plain text and structured elements with Unstructured. PDF, Word, slides, spreadsheets, images.
whenToUse: Read an existing document into text an Agent can work with: a PDF, Word file, slides, spreadsheet, scanned page or a photo of one. It handles digital text and OCR alike, and returns the document broken into titles, paragraphs and tables as well as one plain string. It only READS a file that already exists, so it cannot author or revise one.

inputs.name: file
inputs.description: The document: { downloadUrl } or { content } base64, as S3 Files and Cloudinary emit

outputs.name: text
outputs.description: The whole document as plain text, elements joined in reading order

outputs.description: Structured elements — each with type (Title, NarrativeText, Table), text and metadata

strategy.title: Strategy

chunkingStrategy.title: Chunking
chunkingStrategy.description: Group elements into larger chunks, which is what a RAG pipeline usually wants. Leave as none to get the raw elements.

package.name: unstructured
package.packageFile:
$schema: https://docs.unoverse.ai/schemas/nodes/package.schema.json

# UNSTRUCTURED — one node that reads documents, replacing two that could not be manifests.
#
# WHY THIS EXISTS. Two nodes were stuck for the same reason and neither was worth unsticking:
#
#   DocumentParser   parsed pdf/docx IN PROCESS with `pdf-parse` and `mammoth`. Turning document bytes
#                    into text is local computation, so no amount of "describe the call" reaches it.
#   AmazonTextract   OCR for scanned documents, and blocked on a capability nobody else needed:
#                    paginating a FINISHED job's results by NextToken, on top of an async poll, S3
#                    staging and SigV4 signing. One node, four capabilities.
#
# Unstructured covers both jobs — `strategy: fast` reads a digital PDF the way pdf-parse did, and
# `hi_res`/`ocr_only` reads a scanned one the way Textract did. So this package is not just a migration
# of DocumentParser, it is the reason Textract can be retired rather than migrated, and the reason the
# NextToken pagination never has to be built.
#
# SECOND LIFE (2026-08-04): originally written against the serverless partition endpoint's single
# synchronous POST, which Unstructured has since retired — keys are now issued by the TRANSFORM
# platform (transform.unstructured.io) and refused by the old host. The node now runs the Transform
# job flow (create, poll, download), which is why `poll` joined `multipart` in requires. The output
# element array is unchanged, so nothing downstream noticed.

name: unstructured
displayName: Unstructured
description: Parse documents of any format into text and structured elements
version: 1.0.0
category: ingest
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1785837705/gravity/icons/unstructured_logo.png

features:
  - Parse PDF, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, HTML, images and 20+ other formats into text
  - OCR scanned documents, replacing a dedicated OCR node

allowedHosts:
  - platform-api.transform.unstructured.io
  # ANY HOST, for the UNAUTHENTICATED download only. The node reads a document from a url an upstream node
  # produced — an S3 presigned link, a Cloudinary delivery url — which cannot be declared in advance. That
  # call sends NO credential, and the executor refuses "*" the moment one does, so the wildcard cannot
  # leak this package's api key. Same idiom as aws-bedrock's attachment fetches.
  #
  # It also covers a credential naming its own Unstructured host: a serverless account gets one, and
  # self-hosting gets another. That call DOES send a credential, so it is worth knowing the wildcard does
  # not sanction it — a self-hosted host has to be added here explicitly.
  - "*"

requires:
  executorVersion: ">=1.6.0"
  credential: [apiKeyHeader]
  # `binary` for the optional download of a file given by url, `json` for the job and its output.
  transport: [json, binary]
  encoding: [multipart]
  # A Transform parse is a JOB: without `poll` an executor would settle on the receipt and emit it
  # as the answer, with nothing anywhere reporting a problem.
  poll: true

credentials.unstructuredCredential.yaml:
$schema: https://docs.unoverse.ai/schemas/nodes/credential.schema.json

name: unstructuredCredential
displayName: Unstructured
description: Unstructured API key for document parsing, issued by the Transform platform
documentationUrl: https://docs.unstructured.io/

properties:
  - name: apiKey
    displayName: API Key
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: true
    description: Your Unstructured API key, from transform.unstructured.io (Get started page)
  - name: apiUrl
    displayName: API URL
    type: string
    required: false
    secret: false
    # NOT cosmetic. Unstructured's docs say to use the API URL shown with your key — a self-hosted or
    # enterprise deployment gets its own host. Defaulting silently to the shared host would send
    # documents somewhere the account may not intend.
    description: >-
      Override the API host. Use the URL Unstructured shows next to your key, or your own if
      self-hosting. Defaults to https://platform-api.transform.unstructured.io
    placeholder: https://platform-api.transform.unstructured.io

files.api/run.yaml:
# THE TRANSFORM PLATFORM API, because the synchronous partition endpoint is gone. This node was
# written against api.unstructuredapp.io's one-POST /general/v0/general, and Unstructured retired that
# product: a key issued today comes from transform.unstructured.io and is refused by the old host with
# a 401 that looks like a wrong key rather than a wrong API. Transform is JOB-BASED — create a parsing
# job, poll it, download its output — which is exactly the shape `poll` exists for, and the output that
# comes back is the SAME element array the partition endpoint returned, so everything downstream of
# these calls is unchanged.
#
# THE HOST COMES FROM THE CREDENTIAL, default below is Transform's published one. Any other host must
# also be added to package.yaml allowedHosts, which is the boundary doing its job.
#
# EVERY REQUEST SHAPE HERE WAS PROVED AGAINST THE LIVE API (2026-08-04), not read from docs: the docs
# describe the job flow but not `request_data`, whose key is `job_nodes` and whose node shapes came
# from GET /api/v1/templates/hi_res_partition and trial jobs.

# THE DOWNLOAD, when a url was given rather than bytes.
#
# Transform's create-job takes a FILE PART, not a link, so something has to fetch it — and doing it
# here means a document already in hand as base64 skips this call entirely (`when` leaves no trace
# when false).
#
# NO `auth`, deliberately and necessarily. The url comes from an upstream node and cannot be declared
# in advance, which is why package.yaml allows "*" — and the executor only permits that wildcard for a
# call that sends no credential. Adding auth here would refuse the host rather than leak the key.

- name: download
  when: "return !!String(config.fileUrl || '').trim() && !config.fileBase64"
  method: GET
  url: "{{ config.fileUrl }}"
  # Bytes back as { base64, contentType }, ready to become the file part below.
  transport: binary
  timeoutMs: 120000

# ONE CALL, A JOB. The start POST answers with a receipt ({ id, status: SCHEDULED }), and `poll` asks
# GET /jobs/{id} until COMPLETED — so what this call's name holds is the FINISHED job's information,
# input_file_ids and all, which is what the download below needs.

- name: job
  method: POST
  url: >-
    return (credentials.unstructuredCredential.apiUrl || 'https://platform-api.transform.unstructured.io')
      .replace(/\/+$/, '') + '/api/v1/jobs/'

  credential:
    scheme: apiKeyHeader
    header: unstructured-api-key
    value: "{{ credentials.unstructuredCredential.apiKey }}"

  encoding: multipart

  body:
    # THE FILE PART. `{ base64, mimeType, filename }` is the shape the executor turns back into bytes —
    # the same shape `transport: binary` produces, so a document from S3 Files or Cloudinary flows in
    # without conversion.
    #
    # THE FILENAME MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS. Unstructured chooses its parser from the extension, so a
    # file called `document` with no suffix parses badly and reports no error. That is why `fileName`
    # is a first-class config field rather than a constant.
    input_files: >-
      return (() => {
        const b64 = config.fileBase64 || (calls.download || {}).base64;
        if (!b64) return undefined;
        return { base64: b64,
                 mimeType: (calls.download || {}).contentType || 'application/octet-stream',
                 filename: config.fileName || 'document.pdf' };
      })();

    # THE JOB'S DAG, as a JSON text field (a non-file object part is stringified by the executor,
    # which is how Transform takes it). `job_nodes` builds an ephemeral single-run workflow; the
    # alternative key, `template_id`, names a stock template and cannot carry settings.
    #
    # The node shapes are Transform's workflow vocabulary, proved by trial:
    #   - every strategy except vlm is a `partition/unstructured_api` node whose `settings` take the
    #     same parameters the old endpoint took as form fields (strategy, languages,
    #     include_page_breaks);
    #   - `vlm` is its own SUBTYPE, not a strategy value — `strategy: 'vlm'` inside unstructured_api
    #     settings is refused. Its settings are the vendor's defaults, so languages and page breaks
    #     do not apply on that path;
    #   - chunking is a SECOND NODE in the DAG, not a parameter. The old `basic` behaviour is the
    #     `chunk_by_character` subtype.
    #
    # `languages: undefined` when blank, so OCR auto-detects rather than being told to expect nothing
    # (undefined keys drop out of the stringified part).
    request_data: >-
      return (() => {
        const strat = config.strategy || 'auto';
        const langs = String(config.languages || '').trim()
          ? String(config.languages).split(',').map(l => l.trim()).filter(l => l)
          : undefined;
        const partition = strat === 'vlm'
          ? { name: 'partition', type: 'partition', subtype: 'vlm', settings: {} }
          : { name: 'partition', type: 'partition', subtype: 'unstructured_api',
              settings: { strategy: strat,
                          include_page_breaks: !!config.includePageBreaks,
                          languages: langs } };
        const chunkSubtype = ({ basic: 'chunk_by_character',
                                by_title: 'chunk_by_title',
                                by_page: 'chunk_by_page',
                                by_similarity: 'chunk_by_similarity' })[config.chunkingStrategy];
        const nodes = chunkSubtype
          ? [partition, { name: 'chunk', type: 'chunk', subtype: chunkSubtype, settings: {} }]
          : [partition];
        return { job_nodes: nodes };
      })();

  transport: json
  timeoutMs: 120000

  retry:
    attempts: 3
    backoff: exponential
    on: [429, 500, 502, 503, 504]

  # The API reports refusal in `detail` — a wrong key, a malformed DAG — so it is judged by shape
  # rather than status.
  error:
    when: "return !!response.detail"
    message: >-
      return typeof response.detail === 'string' ? response.detail : JSON.stringify(response.detail)

  # Parsing a long scanned PDF with hi_res or vlm is slow — minutes, not seconds. 5s × 300 attempts
  # is 25 minutes of patience, under the platform's own 300-poll ceiling.
  poll:
    until: "return response.status === 'COMPLETED'"
    failed: "return ['FAILED', 'STOPPED', 'REJECTED'].indexOf(response.status) !== -1"
    message: "return 'Unstructured job ' + response.id + ' ended ' + response.status"
    url: >-
      return (credentials.unstructuredCredential.apiUrl || 'https://platform-api.transform.unstructured.io')
        .replace(/\/+$/, '') + '/api/v1/jobs/' + response.id
    intervalMs: 5000
    maxAttempts: 300

# THE OUTPUT, a separate GET because a finished job holds its result rather than returning it.
# `file_id` is the job's own name for the uploaded document (input_file_ids[0] — there is exactly one,
# this node sends exactly one). No `node_id`: omitted, Transform serves the TERMINAL node's output,
# which is the chunker when one was asked for and the partitioner otherwise.
#
# The reply is the element array itself — the same shape the retired partition endpoint returned —
# and being the last call, it is what `events` reads as `response`.

- name: result
  method: GET
  url: >-
    return (credentials.unstructuredCredential.apiUrl || 'https://platform-api.transform.unstructured.io')
      .replace(/\/+$/, '') + '/api/v1/jobs/' + calls.job.id
      + '/download?file_id=' + encodeURIComponent((calls.job.input_file_ids || [])[0] || '')

  credential:
    scheme: apiKeyHeader
    header: unstructured-api-key
    value: "{{ credentials.unstructuredCredential.apiKey }}"

  transport: json
  timeoutMs: 120000

  error:
    when: "return !!response.detail && !Array.isArray(response)"
    message: >-
      return typeof response.detail === 'string' ? response.detail : JSON.stringify(response.detail)
files.config.yaml:
$schema: https://docs.unoverse.ai/schemas/nodes/config.schema.json

configSchema:
  type: object
  required: [strategy]
  properties:
    fileUrl:
      type: string
      title: File URL
      description: >-
        A URL to fetch the document from. Use this OR File (base64). Usually wired from an upstream node,
        e.g. return signal.s3files1.files[0].downloadUrl
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
    fileBase64:
      type: string
      title: File (base64)
      description: The document itself, base64 encoded, when it is not reachable by URL.
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
    fileName:
      type: string
      title: File Name
      description: >-
        Name including extension, e.g. report.pdf. Unstructured picks its parser from this, so a wrong or
        missing extension is the commonest cause of a poor parse.
      default: document.pdf
      "ui:field": template
    strategy:
      type: string
      title: Strategy
      # REQUIRED, because it is the COST dial as much as the quality one: `fast` reads embedded text and
      # is the cheapest path, while `vlm` runs a vision model over every page and costs an order of
      # magnitude more. Left unset the vendor picks, which is how a large batch quietly becomes expensive.
      # It has a default, so requiring it costs an author nothing — it just makes the choice visible.
      description: >-
        How hard to work. `fast` reads digital text only and is cheapest. `hi_res` runs layout detection
        and OCR, which is what a SCANNED document needs. `ocr_only` forces OCR. `vlm` uses a vision model
        for the hardest layouts. `auto` picks per document.
      enum: [auto, fast, hi_res, ocr_only, vlm]
      enumNames:
        - Auto (pick per document)
        - Fast (digital text only, cheapest)
        - Hi-res (layout + OCR, for scans)
        - OCR only (force OCR)
        - VLM (vision model, hardest layouts)
      default: auto
    chunkingStrategy:
      type: string
      title: Chunking
      description: >-
        Group elements into larger chunks, which is what a RAG pipeline usually wants. Leave as none to
        get the raw elements.
      enum: ["", basic, by_title, by_page, by_similarity]
      enumNames: [None, Basic, By title, By page, By similarity]
      default: ""
    languages:
      type: string
      title: Languages
      description: >-
        Comma-separated OCR language codes, e.g. eng,fra. Only affects the OCR strategies. Leave blank to
        auto-detect.
      default: ""
    includePageBreaks:
      type: boolean
      title: Include Page Breaks
      description: Mark page boundaries in the output
      default: false
      "ui:widget": toggle
"ui:order":
  [fileUrl, fileBase64, fileName, strategy, chunkingStrategy, languages, includePageBreaks]
files.interface.yaml:
$schema: https://docs.unoverse.ai/schemas/nodes/interface.schema.json

inputs:
  - name: file
    type: object
    description: "The document: { downloadUrl } or { content } base64, as S3 Files and Cloudinary emit"
    required: false

outputs:
  - name: text
    type: string
    description: The whole document as plain text, elements joined in reading order
  - name: elements
    type: array
    description: Structured elements — each with type (Title, NarrativeText, Table), text and metadata
  - name: metadata
    type: object
    description: pageCount, elementCount, fileType, tables (as HTML when present)

credentials:
  - name: unstructuredCredential
    required: true
files.node.yaml:
$schema: https://docs.unoverse.ai/schemas/nodes/node.schema.json

type: ParseDocument
kind: PromiseNode

name: Parse Document
category: Documents
color: "#09B29C"
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1785837705/gravity/icons/unstructured_logo.png

description: Read any document into plain text and structured elements with Unstructured. PDF, Word, slides, spreadsheets, images.

# Outcome first, then disqualify by PROPERTY. Doc 14: never name another node — a cross-reference dates
# the moment a node is added or renamed, and ranking surfaces the alternative on its own.
whenToUse: >-
  Read an existing document into text an Agent can work with: a PDF, Word file, slides, spreadsheet,
  scanned page or a photo of one. It handles digital text and OCR alike, and returns the document broken
  into titles, paragraphs and tables as well as one plain string. It only READS a file that already
  exists, so it cannot author or revise one.

# WHO MAY RUN THIS (DECLARATIVE_NODES.md §9.13). Compulsory on every node, so that a node
# nobody thought about cannot look the same as one deliberately left open.
#
# `required: false` adds no requirement of its own: the node runs for whoever the trigger
# admitted. The trigger instance's publicEntry toggle still owns the door, and requirements
# only ever narrow.
auth:
  required: false

capabilities:
  # Parsing IS deterministic for a given file, so cache BY CONTENT IDENTITY, never by URL.
  # `fileUrl` is usually a presigned link (new signature every run over the same bytes), so it
  # is dropped from the fingerprint; the identity is the `etag` an upstream file node delivers.
  # No etag on the inputs → nothing to key on → the run is not cached, which keeps the old
  # caution: a stale transcript of the wrong document is worse than parsing twice.
  cacheable:
    ignore: [fileUrl]
    key: [etag]
files.test.yaml:
$schema: https://docs.unoverse.ai/schemas/nodes/test.schema.json

# Running it live needs UNSTRUCTURED_API_KEY. It reaches the real API and bills per page, so the fixture
# uses a ONE-PAGE public PDF and `strategy: fast` — the cheapest path that still proves the whole chain:
# the url is downloaded, the bytes become a multipart file part, and elements come back.
#
# `fileName` carries the extension deliberately. Unstructured picks its parser from it, so a name without
# one parses badly and reports no error — the single easiest thing to get wrong about this node.

testData:
  config:
    fileUrl: https://www.w3.org/WAI/ER/tests/xhtml/testfiles/resources/pdf/dummy.pdf
    fileName: dummy.pdf
    strategy: fast
  inputs:
    file:
      downloadUrl: https://www.w3.org/WAI/ER/tests/xhtml/testfiles/resources/pdf/dummy.pdf
  expect:
    # REAL TEXT, not merely a string. An empty parse returns [] and would still join to "", which is the
    # failure this has to distinguish from success.
    text: "return typeof output.text === 'string' && output.text.length > 0"
    # ELEMENTS WITH A TYPE. Unstructured's whole value over a plain text dump is the structure, so an
    # element missing `type` means the response shape changed.
    elements: >-
      return Array.isArray(output.elements)
        && output.elements.length > 0
        && typeof output.elements[0].type === 'string'
    metadata: "return output.metadata.elementCount === output.elements.length"
